title: Onboard variant mapping and publish performance signatures for new models
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Create canonical catalog entries and a publishable performance signature for each newly onboarded model variant so that serving, routing, and Console metadata are consistent across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket covers: (1) mapping external model vendor identifiers -> Redwood model_id/variant keys, (2) a deterministic pinning policy for hosted vs dedicated/private, (3) generation and validation of a performance signature JSON (latency, memory, quality markers) and (4) docs updates for the public catalog and internal runbook.

Acceptance criteria:
- A complete model metadata template populated for 3 representative new variants (small, medium-quantized, and full fp16) including fields: model_id, model_family, variant_aliases, architecture, tokenizer, context_window, recommended_batch_size, memory_kv_cache_bytes, quantization_profile, pinned_version, fallback_variants, kernel_profile_hint, perf_signature_s3_path.
- Pinning policy documented and implemented as: hosted -> exact build artifact hash (immutable); dedicated/private -> semantic pinned tag with optional customer-lock flag. Automated check to warn if semantic tag is >30 days old.
- Perf signature generation pipeline implemented (perf-runner job), with outputs pushed to s3://redwood-catalog/perf-signatures/{model_id}/{variant}/{signature-v1}.json and verified against a checksum.
- Docs updated: public catalog page (docs/models.md) with example metadata table row, and internal runbook with how-to for re-running perf-signature and unpinning.
- End-to-end test: create catalog entry from onboarding form, run perf-runner, publish signature, and assert Console shows latencies and recommended batch sizes.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Pinning: We picked exact-hash for hosted to ensure rollback determinism for customer requests and auditability. For Dedicated/Private, semantic tags reduce operator churn for patched builds; to mitigate drift we add a TTL warning and require manual approval before automated rollover.
- Perf signature format: lightweight JSON with numeric metrics (p50/p95 latencies on standard Skylake-1xA100 and Ampere-1xA100G), tokenization variance samples, quality checksums (eval hash against canonical prompt set), and a small matrix of kernel hints. We deliberately avoided storing raw benchmark logs in the signature to keep storage compact; logs go to a separate perf-logs bucket linked by URL.
- Metadata coverage: we include a free-form known_issues field for early-onboard quirks (KV cache growth, OOM patterns) to help solutions engineers.

Implementation plan:
1) Schema: extend catalog schema with variant_aliases, quantization_profile, pinned_version_type, pinned_version_value, perf_signature_path, signature_checksum, last_profiled_at. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/472)
2) Onboarding form: add mapping step to normalize vendor names and capture recommended_batch_size and context_window. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-ui/pull/118)
3) Perf-runner: add runner job and CI step to validate signature JSON against schema and push to S3. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-runner/pull/79)
4) Console: surface perf signature metrics in Catalog detail page and surface pinning warnings. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/629)
5) Runbook: write internal how-to (Confluence link below) and add an automated lint check for new catalog entries.

Artifacts and links:
- Onboarding template (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Model+Onboarding+Template
- Schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/catalog/pull/472
- Perf-runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-runner/pull/79
- Console PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/629
- Example perf signature: s3://redwood-catalog/perf-signatures/example-model/v1/signature-v1.json
- Example onboarding ticket (design notes): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ExampleOnboard

Risk and mitigation:
- Early perf signatures may vary across infra; we will mark first three runs as experimental and not auto-promote to the global catalog until two sequential runs are within 10% of p50. If variance persists, mark variant as 'experimental' in catalog and trigger a follow-up investigation.
- Customer impact if pinned_version rolls inadvertently: add an audit log entry and rollback path that maps to previous signature and artifact hash.

Next steps:
- Engineering: complete PRs for schema and perf-runner and request design review for Console surface.
- Ops: schedule perf-runner nightly for the seed set of models.
- PM: coordinate announcement and update docs page.
